server.arm_p: gap: arm_p.cpp and requests.cpp on Windows. Under MSVC ASan every program that links protoc's generated code stops before main (a null call in protobuf's table-driven parser while the descriptor registers; protobuf's port_def.inc says MSVC cannot guarantee constant initialization of its parse tables). The Linux GCC ASan+UBSan record covers the same source files. clang-cl 22.1.0 ASan runs that code (desktop test, 2026-10-30) but would need LLVM on the laptop; not chosen (Alex, 2026-10-30)

windows.reflection: gap: on Windows only MinGW-w64 GCC 16 builds the reflection layer and arm R, and it has no ASan or UBSan; MSVC and clang-cl have no P2996. The Linux GCC ASan+UBSan and TSan records cover the same first-party inputs (CLAUDE.md D5; p5-typed-endpoints/AGENTS.md line 24)

compile_curve.gate: the compile-curve builds (bench/compile_curve.py) are not CMake builds, so lab/bin/inputs_hash.py cannot hash them. Each build records, untimed, the include/tep/ files its compiles list under g++ -MM with their sha256 (first_party_inputs); each must appear with the same sha256 in the inputs_hash.py --list files of both green GCC sanitizer records, ASan+UBSan and TSan (bench/check_compile_inputs.py exits 0; an R build must list reflect.hpp, and all R builds the same files). Windows compile builds match the Linux records, as the Windows reflection gap above states. Generator P's compiles include no include/tep/ file (Alex, 2026-10-31, "Adopt (Recommended)"; bench/requests/sanitizer-records.md)
compile_curve.generated: gap: the files each build generates (schema.proto and the user program from bench/gen_schema.py; protoc's schema.pb.* for P) are compiled but in no sanitizer record. The measured quantities are the compiler's time and memory; the program's one run is a functional check, not a measurement

request_bodies: gap (2026-11-03, hypotheses-r2.md section 5): server/write_bodies.cpp writes the bodies the load generators send (small, medium and, for the mixed traffic, smaller). It is in no measured target and, since it gained the smaller order after the records of 9a3dc92, in no sanitizer record. Its output is checked instead: every build job checks each body's sha256 against the values in bench/requests/replication.md (small and medium byte for byte the first campaign's), and write_bodies reads each file back and parses it with protobuf before it exits 0

arm_g.scope: arm G (hypotheses-m2.md): arm_g/g_server.cpp, its first-party code, and the e2e.pb.* and e2e.grpc.pb.* that protoc 36.2 and grpc_cpp_plugin generate; Linux only
